selected_candidate.selection_reason: Safest candidate-only first tranche under Gate 6 rubric: smallest non-capital governance surface, direct docs/11 owner/seam mapping, all ten records carry passed_reuse_existing vocabulary posture, no implementation opened, and future work can be bounded to vocabulary governance before any Atlas implementation planning.
selected_candidate.candidate_only_boundary: Proposed for future PM consideration only; not an accepted future tranche, not implementation authority, and no executable leaves are opened.
selected_candidate.vocabulary_posture: No vocabulary mutation in Gate 6. Source slice reports vocabulary_gate_status_counts.passed_reuse_existing=10; future accepted tranche must run the governed vocabulary workflow before admitting or mutating durable terms.
selected_candidate.proof_testing_posture: No proof gate is claimed passed. Source slice requires future Tier A proof/test decisions before any implementation claim.
selected_candidate.dependency_notes: Future accepted tranche package must read docs/10, docs/10.1, docs/vocabulary surfaces, docs/11 §5.18, the vocabulary slice, and current vocabulary tests before planning implementation.
selected_candidate.risk_notes: Candidate-only selection risk is bounded by no implementation, no vocabulary mutation, no schema changes, no generated slice edits, and PM audit before future tranche authorisation.

non_selected_high_ranking_summary.reason_not_selected: Only two records, but capital-deployment authority has high route risk because it is downstream financial authority and would require tighter runtime/proof boundaries than a governance-only first candidate.
High governance leverage, but broader proof-surface blast radius and retained-test/proof interactions make it less safe than vocabulary governance as the first candidate-only tranche.
Useful governance/proof leverage, but persistence/receipt ownership has wider cross-route implications than vocabulary governance.
Smaller record count than many tranches, but live inventory/position state is downstream runtime-sensitive and less route-safe.
Moderate record count, but it sits on a runtime-preparation seam and carries runtime-health dependency burden.
Moderate record count with direct docs/11 mapping, but risk-lane independence and runtime proof boundaries make it less safe for the first candidate-only selection.
